file_description: Daily Oil Production - Average daily oil production rate by field
data_format: WIDE format - one row per field-month with average daily rate
priority: MEDIUM - Useful for validation and rate analysis
use_case: Validate monthly totals, track production rates, calculate uptime/downtime, identify production interruptions

field_descriptions.oil_production_avg_daily_m3: Average daily oil production rate in cubic meters per day (m3/day) for the given month. Arithmetic mean of daily production over all producing days in the month.
field_descriptions.time_index: Year-month identifier in YYYY-MM format for time series analysis
field_descriptions.field_id: Unique field identifier - matches field_id in monthly production and field shapes
field_descriptions.basin: Sedimentary basin (Neuquina, Golfo San Jorge, Austral, Noroeste, Cuyana)

unit_notes.m3_per_day: Cubic meters per day - average daily rate
unit_notes.m3: Cubic meters - if converting to monthly total, multiply by days in month
unit_notes.monthly_validation: To validate: oil_production_avg_daily_m3 * days_in_month ≈ monthly_total_m3 from oil_field_production file

calculated_metrics.monthly_expected_m3: oil_production_avg_daily_m3 * days_in_month - Expected monthly production if running at full capacity
calculated_metrics.production_uptime_fraction: actual_monthly_m3 / (oil_production_avg_daily_m3 * days_in_month) - Fraction of time actually producing. <1.0 indicates downtime.
calculated_metrics.downtime_days_equivalent: (1 - uptime_fraction) * days_in_month - Equivalent days of downtime in the month
calculated_metrics.is_intermittent_production: uptime_fraction < 0.7 - Binary flag for fields with significant downtime

data_quality_validation.monthly_total_check: Compare daily avg * days to monthly total from oil_field_production file. Should match within ~5% unless significant downtime.
data_quality_validation.zero_production: Zero values may indicate: (1) field shut-in, (2) maintenance, (3) no production that month, (4) data not reported
data_quality_validation.outlier_detection: Sudden spikes or drops in daily rate month-to-month may indicate: workovers, new wells online, equipment failure, or data errors
data_quality_validation.consistency_check: Daily rate should be relatively stable unless new wells added or significant changes. Large variations warrant investigation.

technical_notes.average_calculation: This is arithmetic mean of daily production over the month. Does not account for days with zero production vs no production.
technical_notes.uptime_analysis: Comparing daily average to monthly total reveals production uptime. Mature fields often have 80-95% uptime. Newer fields may be higher.
technical_notes.rate_vs_volume: Daily rate (m3/day) measures intensity of production. Monthly volume (m3) measures total production. Both needed for complete analysis.
technical_notes.validation_importance: Cross-checking daily rates against monthly totals is critical quality control. Mismatches indicate data errors or downtime.
technical_notes.decline_curve_analysis: Daily rates more useful for decline curve analysis than monthly totals. Shows production rate changes over time.
technical_notes.comparison_to_us_units: US oilfield uses bbl/day (barrels per day) instead of m3/day. 1 m3/day = 6.28981 bbl/day.
technical_notes.downtime_causes: Common causes of reduced uptime: equipment maintenance, well workovers, pipeline/facility shutdowns, regulatory restrictions, seasonal weather impacts.

data_integration.join_key: field_id + year + month - join to monthly production data
validation_workflow: 3. Calculate expected monthly = daily avg * days in month
6. Flag fields with uptime < 70% for investigation
data_integration.complementary_data: Use with monthly production totals to calculate uptime, identify production interruptions, and validate data quality

use_cases.data_validation: Primary use is validating monthly production totals. Daily avg * days should match monthly total within 5-10%.
use_cases.uptime_calculation: Calculate field operating uptime by comparing actual monthly to expected (daily * days). Identify reliability issues.
use_cases.rate_analysis: Track production rate trends over time. Identify decline rates, new well impacts, workover effectiveness.
use_cases.anomaly_detection: Sudden changes in daily rate indicate production events: well additions, failures, workovers, or data errors.
use_cases.operator_performance: Compare uptime across operators to identify best practices and reliability differences.

limitations.no_well_level: This is field-level average only. Does not show individual well contributions.
limitations.averaging_masks_detail: Daily average smooths out intra-month variation. Doesn't show when production occurred.
limitations.zero_ambiguity: Zero production could mean shut-in field or missing data. Cannot distinguish without additional info.
limitations.no_gas_equivalent: Only oil has daily average data. No equivalent file for gas production rates.

typical_values.small_field_m3_day: 10-100 m3/day typical for small conventional field with 5-20 wells
typical_values.medium_field_m3_day: 100-1000 m3/day for medium conventional field or small Vaca Muerta development
typical_values.large_field_m3_day: 1000-10000 m3/day for large conventional field or significant Vaca Muerta field
typical_values.giant_field_m3_day: >10000 m3/day for major fields. Top Argentina fields produce 20000+ m3/day.
typical_values.expected_uptime: Mature fields: 80-95%. New fields: 90-98%. Fields <70% uptime indicate issues.

example_analysis.validation_check_python: is_valid = abs(monthly_total_m3 - daily_avg_m3 * days_in_month) / monthly_total_m3 < 0.10  # Within 10%
